proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current formulation does not type the represented model classes by the derived input-free COPAG and does not separate finite positive-rational membership from binary-certificate membership. The repaired claim derives the COPAG from the common extended graph and requires binary support for every endogenous and latent base variable before concluding binary-subclass membership.

prose_updates.honest_scope: No selected conditional completeness theorem is claimed. Branch-sCIDP soundness is stated over the published positive discrete class and allows countable discrete coordinate supports; because the observed vertex set is finite, every joint outcome assignment space used in normalization is at most countable. The affine compiler and the explicit tabular witnesses lie unconditionally in the positive rational binary subclass. The generic selection-equalizer lift instead supplies a positive rational finite witness in the published discrete class. Under its common-graph and active-parent hypotheses, the model classes are indexed by the input-free COPAG \(\mathcal P^+\) represented by the selected projection of the common extended graph, rather than by that graph itself. The lift lies in the positive rational binary subclass only when every endogenous and latent variable of each base SCM is binary; the appended private noises can then also be chosen binary. Without that support hypothesis, the lift does not itself yield a binary certificate pair. A countermodel pair in the binary subclass refutes identification in the larger class, but this negative transfer supplies no positive completeness implication. The affine rank equivalence is conditional on a specified perturbation interval that remains in the represented class. The connected table proves nonvacuity and the same-graph perturbation proves that its lock is not structural. The implication from all reachable terminal failures to a represented residual forest with a locked rational pair, together with the advertised synthesis bound, remains exactly the graph-to-lock open question. Continuous variables, intervention inputs, faithfulness-only claims, and general finite-alphabet certificate completeness are outside scope.
